su.title: Shared Understanding (+ answers.md, espelho _graph/)
su.authority: shared-understanding.md is the single authority for claims and their epistemic state (library/kernel/states.md:3; .claude/rules/shared-understanding-as-source-of-truth.md:3-7); answers.md keeps the verbatim answers (states.md:67) and is a locator target for Confirmed (states.md:30-32). _graph/ is a mirror that must never prevail (graph.py:30-35, drift() 222-264: state/criticidade/resolved block, text informs), BUT bootstrap.py blocks readiness on AUTHORITY_DRIFT / AUTHORITY_UNMIRRORED / LEGACY_MODE (bootstrap.py:306-317, 336-362), and bootstrap readiness gates every coordinator writer and the Write/Edit guard — so every SU writer must keep the mirror in step. Publication mechanism is operation.py run() (intent -> pending marker -> temp+rename -> verify -> receipt, flock exclusion; operation.py:465-577). Only resolve.py (answer + 4 lifecycle ops + sync_mirror) and migrate.py publish SU/answers/graph through it; all other SU writers are direct Write/Edit tool edits mirrored post-hoc by the on-su-mirror PostToolUse hook. The normative kernel contracts (states.md, phases.md, orchestration.md, glossary.md) never mention the graph, mirror, coordinator or bootstrap (grep over those files returned no hits); the writer protocol lives only in engine code, CLAUDE.md:29-33 and .claude/hooks/HOOKS.md:8-14.

wrong.claimed: path_patterns: 'next version formatted v{:02d} (coverage.py:3606-3612); one counter shared by all three stages'
wrong.corrected: next_version is not a monotonic counter. It takes the LOWEST unused number (n=1; while n in taken: n+=1). Once any record is removed, whether by finalize's own changed-during unlink or by hand-deleting a torn record (the only recovery), the next finalize fills the gap. The newer review then gets a lower version than an older one. load_records and select_record order by version number and pick the highest as 'latest', so the newer review is silently treated as superseded.
